info.name: ImageFX
info.comment: Renders a bitmap image in the effect pipeline.

description.p: The ImageFX class will render a source image into a given rectangle within the current user coordinate system. The client has the option of providing a pre-allocated Bitmap or the path to a Image file as the source.

A pre-allocated bitmap is assigned to the Bitmap field, or it can be created as a child of the uninitialised ImageFX. The bitmap must be initialised before it is assigned, or before the ImageFX is initialised in the case of a child. The default IMAGE mode requires 32 bits per pixel with an alpha channel. The ImageFX keeps the bitmap alive until it is replaced or the ImageFX is freed; an attempt to free it earlier is deferred. Source images loaded from a Path are converted to the required format automatically.

The source can be replaced at any time, including after initialisation. Setting Path loads a new image file, and setting Bitmap binds a different bitmap. A replacement that fails, for instance because the file cannot be read or the current ViewBox does not fit inside the new image, leaves the previous source active. Use Reload to read the file at Path again after it has been modified on disk.
Changes to the pixels of a bound bitmap are not detected automatically. Call Refresh() on the ImageFX after editing the bitmap in place, so that buffered viewports that use the filter are redrawn.

Set ViewBox to render a section of the bitmap, such as one cell of an image atlas. The selected pixels are fitted to the primitive subregion according to AspectRatio, and resampling clamps to the edges of the section so that neighbouring pixels do not bleed into the result.

Setting OutputMode to HEIGHT produces a floating-point map for effects such as TileFX and LightingFX. A BMF::GREYSCALE bitmap supplies its full 16-bit samples, including when loaded from a 16-bit greyscale PNG. For other formats, HeightChannel selects the stored channel to read, with red as the default. Heights are normalised to the range 0 to 1 and resampled without colour-space conversion.

Technically the ImageFX object is represented by a new viewport, the bounds of which are defined by attributes X, Y, Width and Height. The placement and scaling of the referenced image is controlled by the AspectRatio field.

action.name: Draw
action.comment: Render the effect to the target bitmap.
action.prototype: ERR acDraw(*Object, DOUBLE X, DOUBLE Y, DOUBLE Width, DOUBLE Height)

input.param: The X position of the region to be drawn.
The Y position of the region to be drawn.
The width of the region to be drawn.
The height of the region to be drawn.

action.name: Refresh
action.comment: Redraws filter clients after the pixels of the source bitmap are changed.

description.p: The ImageFX cannot detect edits to the pixels of its source Bitmap. Call Refresh after editing them so that buffered viewports that use the filter discard their cached content. Changes to the fields of the ImageFX are detected automatically and do not need a Refresh.
Refresh does not read the source file again; use Reload for that. It also does not schedule drawing.

method.name: Reload
method.comment: Reloads the image file referenced by Path.

description.p: Reload reads the file at Path again and replaces the current image with its new content. Use it when the file has been modified since it was loaded. The ViewBox, OutputMode and the document-relative reference used for SVG export are retained.
If the file cannot be loaded, or the ViewBox does not fit inside the new image, the previous image remains active.
Controls how the source image, or the section of it selected by ViewBox, is aligned and scaled to fit the primitive subregion. The default is X_MID|Y_MID|MEET.

field.name: Bitmap
field.comment: The Bitmap being used as the image source.

description.p: Reading the Bitmap field returns the Bitmap that is being used as the image source. If an image has been loaded from Path, the Bitmap refers to the content of that image.

Writing to the Bitmap field replaces the current source with a client-supplied Bitmap. The field can be set before or after initialisation, and buffered viewports that use the filter are redrawn on their next draw. Any image previously loaded from Path is released, and Path reads as empty from then on.

The ImageFX pins the bitmap so that it remains valid while it is the source. An attempt to free the bitmap in the meantime is deferred until it is replaced or the ImageFX is freed. The ImageFX does not detect changes to the bitmap's pixels; call Refresh() after editing them.

field.name: HeightChannel
field.comment: Selects the stored channel to read in height mode.

description.p: A 16-bit greyscale bitmap supplies its grey samples regardless of this setting. For other bitmaps, alpha reads as 1 when the bitmap has no alpha channel.

field.name: OutputMode
field.comment: Selects image or floating-point height output.

description.p: The default IMAGE mode renders the source as colour. The HEIGHT mode produces a floating-point map from the channel selected by HeightChannel, for consumption by effects such as LightingFX. The mode can only be set before initialisation. If an image has already been loaded from Path, it is loaded again in the format that the new mode requires.

field.name: Path
field.comment: Path to an image file supported by the Image class.

description.p: Setting the Path loads the referenced file as the image source, replacing any existing source. The path can be set before or after initialisation. The image is converted to the format that OutputMode requires.
Reading the Path returns an empty string if the source is a client bitmap. SVG export requires a path relative to the document folder.

field.name: ResampleMethod
field.comment: The resample algorithm to use for transforming the source image.

field.name: ViewBox
field.comment: Selects a section of the source bitmap, in pixels.

description.p: By default the entire source bitmap is rendered. Set ViewBox to an array of four values, { x, y, width, height }, to render only a section of it, such as one cell of an image atlas. The section is fitted to the primitive subregion according to AspectRatio, as if it were the whole image. Unlike the viewBox of an SVG viewport, the section is a strict crop: resampling clamps to its edges, so pixels outside of it never contribute to the result.

All values must be whole numbers, the width and height must be greater than zero, and the rectangle must lie inside the current source bitmap if one is set. Otherwise the new value is rejected with ERR::OutOfRange and the current rectangle is retained. An array that does not have four values is rejected with ERR::InvalidValue.
Set an empty array, or a zero width and height, to clear the rectangle. Reading the field returns an empty array when no rectangle is set.
If the source bitmap shrinks after the rectangle is set so that it no longer fits, drawing the effect fails with ERR::OutOfRange.
In SVG, the equivalent attribute is xvg:viewBox="x y width height" on the feImage element.

field.name: XMLDef
field.comment: Describes the primitive using the FilterEffect.XMLDef format.

The blue channel.
The green channel, which is the roughness channel of a packed ORM map.

The red channel. This is the default, and the occlusion channel of a packed ORM map.
Selects a resampling method automatically. The choice depends on the operation.
Uses a broad Bessel filter that can preserve detail during resampling, but is slower than the smaller-kernel methods.
Produces a similar result to BILINEAR at a slightly higher CPU cost and a marginally sharper after-effect.
Bilinear is a common algorithm that produces a reasonable quality image quickly.
Five times slower than BILINEAR, the final result will be less sharp than SINC.
Uses a Gaussian filter that softens the result, reducing aliasing at the cost of sharp edge detail.
Uses a Kaiser-windowed filter, giving smooth interpolation with low ringing and a cost close to BILINEAR.
This well known algorithm may serve as a point of comparison for evaluating the results of other methods. It shares characteristics with SINC and BLACKMAN.
Uses a Mitchell-Netravali filter, balancing sharpness and smoothness at a cost similar to BICUBIC.
Nearest neighbour is the fastest sampler at the cost of poor quality.
Uses a quadratic filter with a modest kernel, giving smoother results than BILINEAR with limited extra cost.
Five times slower than BILINEAR, the final result is of very good quality.

About twice as slow as BILINEAR, this method samples a 4x4 area and produces a considerably better result, and is a good choice for enlarging images without producing artifacts when contrasting colours are present.
